title: Saving Water in the Driest Place on Earth

blanks.sentence: Growing food is becoming harder as climate change increases _____.
Farming uses _____ of the world's fresh water supply.
During a severe drought, date farmers have had to draw water from _____.
Gaps in sandy soil cause rapid _____ of water.
This makes it hard for a plant to establish its _____.
Clay has _____ that stick together, helping the soil retain water.
According to the maker, the treatment creates a habitat in which _____ can develop.
By changing the soil, the clay-and-water mixture promotes _____ in trees.
Its maker expects most farmers to recover their _____ within two years.
According to its maker, the mixture contains clay, air and water, with _____.
blanks.section: The maker's account of the ingredients

multipleChoice.question: Why is improving water use in farming presented as an important issue?
options: Farming has made river water permanently unusable.
Date farms produce less food than other farms.
Farming uses much fresh water while droughts threaten food growing.
Household drinking water is the main source of irrigation.

multipleChoice.question: What makes the drought in Yuma especially severe in the account?
options: It is described as the area's worst in five centuries.
It has already forced all date farms to close.
It has spread from Yuma across every US state.
It has stopped rivers from carrying any water.

multipleChoice.question: What effect do the liquid's makers claim for sandy desert soil?
options: It supplies all the nutrients plants need to make.
It removes the need for a plant's root system.
It changes the weather immediately around farms.
It helps the ground hold water and nutrients.

multipleChoice.question: Why is the habitat for soil microbiology significant in the maker's explanation?
options: It prevents all future changes to the soil.
It may help soil life and natural processes develop.
It replaces the need for any water in the soil.
It proves the mixture works in every desert.

multipleChoice.question: What financial tradeoff is described for farmers considering the technique?
options: A low setup price comes with high annual fees.
An immediate profit comes with a shorter harvest.
A substantial initial cost may be recovered within two years.
A free trial may lead to permanent equipment costs.

multipleChoice.question: What water-saving benefit does the maker claim for fruit trees?
options: They could need half as much water to grow.
They could grow without any water at all.
They could produce twice as many fruits with no change in water.
They could be protected from half of future droughts.

multipleChoice.question: What concern is raised about changing the soil in this way?
options: The technique has already damaged nearby farms.
Harmful effects might emerge later.
The mixture will stop natural processes immediately.
The soil will become too expensive for other uses.

multipleChoice.question: What overall conclusion is best supported by the claimed benefits and the later caution?
options: The water savings prove it is a permanent solution.
The named ingredients guarantee it is safe over time.
Its initial cost means it cannot help any farmers.
Its long-term value remains uncertain despite the claims.
